==English==
{{wp|<dab!>}}

===Etymology===
{{ety|en|:bor|fr:plan<id:map>}}
{{bor+|en|fr|plan|t=flat surface, ground plot, map}}, from {{der|en|la|plānus}}. Some sources also argue for influence or alteration of {{der|en|fr|plant}}, from {{m|fr|plantar}}, from {{der|en|la|plantāre|t=set, fix in place}}. {{doublet|en|llano|piano|plane|plain}}.

===Pronunciation===
* {{enPR|plăn}}
* {{IPA|en|/plæn/|a=RP,GA}}
** {{IPA|en|[pleən]|~|[plɛən]|a=GA,/æ/ tensing}}
*** {{audio|en|en-us-plan.ogg|a=US|IPA=[plɛən]}}
* {{IPA|en|/plan/|a=SSB,Northern England,Scotland,Wales}}
* {{IPA|en|/plæːn/|a=AU!Australia}}
** {{IPA|en|[pleːn]|~|[plɛːn]|a=AU!Australia,/æ/ tensing}}
* {{IPA|en|/plɛn/|a=NZ}}
* {{rhymes|en|æn|s=1}}

===Noun===
{{en-noun}}

# {{senseid|en|drawing}} A [[drawing]] showing technical details of a [[building]], [[machine]], etc., with unwanted details omitted, and often using symbols rather than detailed drawing to represent [[door]]s, [[valve]]s, etc.
#: {{syn|en|design|scheme|Thesaurus:diagram}}
#: {{ux|en|The '''plans''' for many important buildings were once publicly available.}}
# {{senseid|en|intention}} A set of [[intend]]ed actions, usually mutually related, through which one expects to achieve a [[goal]].
#: {{syn|en|design|scheme|Thesaurus:design}}
#: {{ux|en|He didn't really have a '''plan'''; he had a goal and a habit of control.}}
# {{senseid|en|floor plan}} A two-[[dimension]]al drawing of a building as seen from above with obscuring or irrelevant details such as [[roof]] removed, or of a [[floor]] of a building, revealing the internal layout; as distinct from the [[elevation]].
#: {{syn|en|floor plan}}
#: {{ux|en|Seen in '''plan''', the building had numerous passageways not apparent to visitors.}}
# {{senseid|en|method}} A [[method]]; a way of procedure; a [[custom]].
#* {{quote-book|en|year=1815|author=w:William Wordsworth|title=[[s:Poems (Wordsworth, 1815)/Volume 2/Rob Roy's Grave|Rob Roy's Grave]]
|passage=The simple '''plan''', / That they should take who have the power, / And they should keep who can.}}
# {{senseid|en|subscription}} A [[subscription]] to a [[service]].
#: {{ux|en|a phone '''plan'''}}
#: {{ux|en|an Internet '''plan'''}}

====Usage notes====
* A plan ("set of intended actions") can be developed, executed, implemented, ignored, abandoned, scrapped, changed, etc.

===Verb===
{{en-verb}}

# {{senseid|en|design}} {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[design]] (a building, machine, etc.).
#: {{ux|en|The architect '''planned''' the building for the client.}}
# {{senseid|en|trans-plan}} {{lb|en|transitive}} To create a plan for.
#: {{ux|en|They jointly '''planned''' the project in phases, with good detail for the first month.}}
# {{senseid|en|intend}} {{lb|en|intransitive}} To [[intend]].
#: {{ux|en|He '''planned''' to go, but work intervened.}}
#* {{RQ:Economist|date=2013-08-10|volume=408|issue=8848
|title=[http://www.economist.com/news/leaders/21583277-worlds-biggest-polluter-going-green-it-needs-speed-up-transition-can-china Can China clean up fast enough?]
|passage=It has jailed environmental activists and is '''planning''' to limit the power of judicial oversight by handing a state-approved body a monopoly over bringing environmental lawsuits.}}
# {{senseid|en|intrans-plan}} {{lb|en|intransitive}} To make a plan.
#: {{ux|en|They '''planned''' for the worst, bringing lots of emergency supplies.}}

====Usage notes====
* This is a [[catenative]] verb that takes the ''to infinitive''. See [[Appendix:English catenative verbs]].
